clue.text: Clergyman served up opening drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the clergyman's title is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title
an opening is a mouth, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: A vicar sets out the aperitif before the meal begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified, herb-flavoured wine is a kind of drink, often taken as an aperitif.

clue.text: Preliminary passion

definitions.meaning: a preliminary round of a race or contest, the one that decides who goes through to the final
intense feeling, as in 'in the ___ of the moment'

explanation.surface: Foreplay before the main event, or so it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a qualifying round in athletics, and strong anger or ardour.

clue.text: Took views overheard before first sign of danger

indicators.note: overheard tells us to take what a word sounds like when spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: views as a verb means sees

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a threat and acted before it showed itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something forcibly is to grab hold of it; past tense matches the clue's past tense.

clue.text: Admire spa from a very small vessel

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it admiringly
Bath is the English spa town famous for its Roman baths

explanation.surface: A tourist gazes at a spa resort, seen from a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a tiny cup for rinsing the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: This little cup shaped to fit the eye socket is literally a very small container for liquid.

clue.text: Matching degree course

definitions.meaning: running alongside and corresponding, as in similar cases
a line of latitude, measured in degrees, running round the globe

explanation.surface: A university offers a programme that corresponds to another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degree course' reads as university study; it is a circle of latitude named by its degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of latitude are called by this name, and equally the word means similar or corresponding.

clue.text: Leave Ted behind for adventuresome tripping, involving lots of shifting about

indicators.note: tripping suggests stumbling about, so the letters of the long word are jumbled
Leave with behind says the letters of the name are left out of the pool
behind completes leave behind, the instruction to drop the name's letters

explanation.surface: Ted is left at home while his daring friends go off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, E, D from ADVENTURESOME and rearrange the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Military or tactical movements involve a great deal of moving and repositioning.

clue.text: Film about collaboration between Goering and Hitler

indicators.note: the answer is formed by the two names working together, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: A documentary on how two Nazi leaders worked together.
explanation.walkthrough: The film sits in the end of 'Goering', the word 'and' and the start of 'Hitler'; 'about' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Attenborough's 1982 biopic of the Indian independence leader won the Best Picture Oscar.

clue.text: Where one might well end up introducing quantifier into Anglican year

definitions.text: Where one might well end up

indicators.note: introducing one thing into another means placing it within
into marks the outer pair of pieces that receive the measuring word

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church
a meter is a device that measures quantity, as for gas or water

explanation.surface: A church calendar gets a new measuring device in its year.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial ground is the final resting place where everyone may finish, a wry euphemism.

clue.text: Filipino crop a bit in front by this summer

indicators.note: by means next to, so the single letter sits beside the shortened frame
only the bit in front of the counting frame is used, its tail dropped

parts.note: a summer is something that sums or adds up, as a counting frame with beads does

explanation.surface: A farmer in the Philippines plans his harvest ahead of the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but an adder: the abacus. Take its front part, ABAC, and put A beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila hemp is a fibre plant grown chiefly in the Philippines, so it is that country's crop.

clue.text: Obscenities begin to be uttered after sadomasochism

indicators.note: after places the opening of the spoken word behind the two-letter abbreviation

parts.note: SM is the usual short form of sadomasochism

indicators.note: begin to be uttered asks for only the opening of that word

explanation.surface: Filthy words start to come out once the conversation turns kinky.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters, UT, of 'uttered' are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty talk and indecent material are both called by this word, a mass noun for obscene matter.

clue.text: Booze draws drunk into trees

indicators.note: drunk suggests something staggering out of order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Alcohol lures inebriated people into the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Several tropical hardwood species with striped timber go by this name, so they are trees.

clue.text: Dived without a springboard and hurtled forward

indicators.note: the springboard is the starting point from which a diver leaps, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to dive is to plunge into water

explanation.surface: A diver with no board to bounce from simply threw himself forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing oneself suddenly forwards, as a fencer does, is to make a thrust or rush.

clue.text: Cosy gropes possible with these navigational aids!

indicators.note: possible suggests one possible arrangement of the letters among many

explanation.surface: A cheeky note that snug fumbling is feasible using these devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning stabilisers are used in compasses and autopilots to help ships and aircraft keep course.

clue.text: A mild TUC review is as from a sacred text

indicators.note: a review is a looking over again, here a reordering of the letters

explanation.surface: A gentle report from the Trades Union Congress is treated as scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the body of Jewish law and commentary, a holy book.

clue.text: Ah Harpo! Possibly one of the greats of yesteryear

definitions.text: one of the greats of yesteryear

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Addressing the silent Marx brother as a comic legend of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptian rulers were among the mightiest figures of the distant past.

clue.text: Sort of "bandit person" bearing a weapon

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one should'
carrying a gun is being armed

explanation.surface: An armed robber is a kind of bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine, named for its single lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Slot machines are nicknamed this kind of bandit from their lever and their habit of taking money.

clue.text: Prime minister abandons dodgy poolrooms for a sherry

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something unsound, so the remaining letters are shuffled
abandons says the abbreviation's letters are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A politician leaves seedy billiard halls in favour of a glass of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P and M out of POOLROOMS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark, full-bodied Spanish fortified wine is a style of sherry.

clue.text: Part when equal bottom — about the last chance

indicators.note: about means around, so the bottom goes round the equal

parts.note: a seat is one's bottom
par means equal, as in on a par

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Players who finish level must split up before the final opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to divide or go different ways, a verb synonym.

clue.text: They label back to front to confound

indicators.note: the letter at the back is brought round to the front

parts.note: people who tag or label things are taggers

explanation.surface: Labellers who get things back to front cause confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or bewilder someone is to amaze them, as a shock does.

clue.text: Simplest production, where characters have been cast badly

definitions.text: where characters have been cast badly

indicators.note: a production is a staging, here a new staging of the letters

explanation.surface: A very basic theatre show with poorly chosen actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' and 'cast' look theatrical, but they mean letters set down wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly written word has its letters set out wrongly, which is the clue's jokey stage picture.

clue.text: Instinctive move to eat at pub

indicators.note: at here places the shuffled word right after the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: move tells us the letters of the word for eating shift around

explanation.surface: Gut feeling says go and have a meal in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn qualities are natural and not learned, which is what instinctive means.

clue.text: This habit would not be adopted by Conrad, for instance

definitions.text: This habit would not be adopted by Conrad, for instance

parts.words: This habit would not be adopted by Conrad, for instance
parts.note: the novelist Conrad already had this first name, so it needed no adopting as a pen name; habit also suggests the coat of many colours

explanation.surface: A writer would never take up a particular custom.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Conrad's given first name was kept when he anglicised his Polish name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish-born author of Heart of Darkness was named Joseph, so the forename was his own already.

clue.text: Teased short girl over cast-off

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the girl's name above the next piece

parts.note: Jo is a short form of girls' names such as Joanna
to cast off is to shed, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A little girl was mocked about her hand-me-down clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Joking with someone playfully is ribbing or teasing them.

clue.text: They trail along behind — hospital department hours being trimmed a long time

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: trimmed means cut at both ends, leaving the middle

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Staff follow a clinic team whose shifts were cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinues of attendants follow an important person, trailing along after them.

clue.text: This party starts otherwise with fish

indicators.note: starts otherwise means the party's opening letter is changed to another

parts.note: Tory is the name of the UK Conservative party

explanation.surface: A political party opens differently by serving fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces T; the fish name settles it as D.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dory is an edible sea fish, often just called by the second name.

clue.text: Provides the odd steroid from the east

indicators.note: reading from the east is reading right to left, so the letters are turned round
the odd letters are the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: An occasional drug supply arrives from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of STEROID give SEOD, which is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone a meal is to provide it, a colloquial sense of the verb.

clue.text: That's the place to take a line off the record

indicators.note: take with off says a stretch of letters is removed
off completes take off, the instruction to remove

parts.note: a coincidence, not a hidden word: these words lose the line from their end, leaving only their front
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: A journalist withdraws a quote so it is no longer on the record.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb points to a location other than here, so it names a place.

clue.text: How the weather can heat kettles

definitions.meaning: the forces of nature such as wind and rain, as in braving them
the electric heating coils inside kettles

explanation.surface: Wondering how the weather could bring a kettle to the boil.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are common: the weather as nature's forces, and electric heating coils.
